scope: Calico IPv4 NetworkPolicy TCP/HTTP and DNS acceptance on owned kind nodes
working_tree: Uncommitted implementation; verify per-phase source hashes

calico_lock.scope: Fresh owned kind cluster only; no CNI replacement in existing clusters; standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicy TCP/DNS functional acceptance

observations: The Calico profile is created with kindnet disabled. Control-plane bootstrap finishes as network_pending; ordinary Jobs and runtime probes remain gated until CNI readiness.
Upstream YAML is checksum-verified, parsed by pinned kubectl, then rendered to digest-pinned JSON with owned labels and explicit IPv4 VXLAN settings. No extra Python runtime dependency is needed.
kubectl client dry-run emits a JSON stream for multiple YAML documents; the parser accepts both streams and Lists.
CoreDNS can exceed its historical rollout deadline while CNI is absent. Readiness uses its current Available condition without changing its configuration or restarting it.

Both ordinary and gVisor Pods pass the same cross-node 22-case matrix through baseline, default deny, selected allow, revoke and restore. New connections and target identity prevent closed listeners, stale replies or local DNS caches from counting as successful policy enforcement.

Creation and installation used evolving development code. Each phase source hash is retained; final traffic probe programs, policies, topology and CNI definition match accepted inputs. The last host-side change permits owned cleanup after desired kind configuration changes and is covered by regression.
The existing gVisor worker-wide systemd MemorySwapMax policy remains explicit. CNI verification does not claim complete runtime accounting or production reliability.
Policy fixtures exist only in run-scoped test namespaces and are removed after acceptance; this does not install default-deny rules for ordinary tasks or future sessions.
not_validated: Agent Sandbox sessions or warm pools
